report.summary: File defines lint.py: computes DOM/CSSOM metrics from probe.js captures. Exports analyse(), compare(), main(), and helper functions. Docstrings claim Tier A/B separation, no pixel inspection, stdlib-only, and threshold status; all checkable claims are kept or uncheckable.
risks: analyse() line 107 | medium | contrast_ratio may fail if fg/bg keys missing; only guarded by 'fg' in e but not 'bgEff' | Add guard for 'bgEff' in e
analyse() line 201 | medium | _looks_like_identifier uses .isalnum() which fails on non-ASCII; may miss leaks | Document or handle non-ASCII
main() line 249 | low | Writes to runs/gui/report.json without checking if file exists; might overwrite | Add confirmation or append mode
compare() line 228 | low | Asserts reports[0]["metrics"] exists; crashes on empty reports | Add guard for empty reports

handoff.purpose: Define metrics computation and comparison for GUI linting from probe.js captures.

claims.text: No pixels are inspected; every number here is derived from geometry and computed style
claims.why: All metrics use element geometry (x,y,w,h) and computed style (font, color, etc.) from the capture; no pixel data is referenced.

claims.text: Tier A metrics (contrast, overflow, target size, banned faces) measure things that are true or false
claims.why: Contrast_failures, horizontal_overflow, small_targets, banned_faces, console_errors are computed with clear thresholds and boolean conditions.

claims.text: Tier B metrics are PROXIES for a judgement no rule can make
claims.why: Metrics like visible_elements, framed_panels, distinct_radii, etc. are explicitly marked tier B and described as proxies.

claims.text: Every metric returns its count AND the elements behind it
claims.why: Metric dataclass has 'offenders' field; all metric instances in analyse() include element lists.

claims.text: Thresholds are stamped ASSUMED until the corpus is large enough to earn MEASURED
claims.why: No threshold values or their status (ASSUMED/MEASURED) are defined in this chunk; thresholds are hardcoded (e.g., 4.5:1, 44x44) but not labeled.

claims.text: Right now the corpus is n=4 (three rejected surfaces, one approved)
claims.why: No corpus or sample data is present in this file; cannot verify claim.

claims.text: stdlib only, by design
claims.why: Imports: json, math, collections.Counter, dataclasses, pathlib.Path — all stdlib.

claims.text: BANNED_FACES = ("inter", "roboto", "arial", "space grotesk", "geist", "helvetica neue")
claims.why: Literal definition present.

claims.text: Text that is a leaked internal name rather than something a person would say.
claims.why: Function implements heuristic to detect such text.

claims.text: A framed surface, not a hairline divider or a text run.
claims.why: Function checks borderSides >=1, w>=56, h>=24.

claims.text: the page body must never scroll sideways
claims.why: Metric horizontal_overflow computed as max(0, scrollWidth - clientWidth).

claims.text: WCAG AA: 4.5:1 body, 3.0:1 large
claims.why: Contrast thresholds applied: large text >=18px or bold >=14px -> 3.0, else 4.5.

claims.text: interactive targets should reach 44x44
claims.why: Metric small_targets counts elements where w<44 or h<44.

claims.text: grotesk defaults that mark a generated page
claims.why: BANNED_FACES list includes those faces; metric counts occurrences.

claims.text: a broken page is not a design question
claims.why: Metric console_errors counts errors from capture.

claims.text: raw density of what is on screen at once
claims.why: Metric visible_elements uses cap['elementsKept'].

claims.text: when everything is a bordered box, nothing is elevated
claims.why: Metric framed_panels counts panels; comment explains.

claims.text: more than two or three corner radii reads as unconsidered
claims.why: Metric distinct_radii counts distinct radius values.

claims.text: frames inside frames inside frames
claims.why: Metric panel_nesting_depth computed via geometric containment.

claims.text: shouted micro-labels used as decoration rather than hierarchy
claims.why: Metric allcaps_text_share counts uppercase text.

claims.text: if everything is flagged, nothing is flagged
claims.why: Metric status_pills_visible counts pill-shaped elements.

claims.text: an N-equal-tile metric row is the most recognisable trope in the category
claims.why: Metric largest_equal_tile_row computed via grouping by y and size similarity.

claims.text: distinct 30-degree hue families in use, semantic colour included
claims.why: Metric accent_hue_families counts hue buckets.

claims.text: internal field names and raw JSON rendered as user-facing text
claims.why: Metric identifier_leaks uses _looks_like_identifier heuristic.

claims.text: do the numbers separate the surfaces a human rejected from the one he approved?
claims.why: Function exists but no human verdicts are present in this chunk; functionality depends on external data.

observations.what: analyse() uses 'bgEff' key but only checks 'fg' in e before accessing; may cause KeyError if 'bgEff' missing.
_looks_like_identifier uses .isalnum() which fails on non-ASCII (e.g., underscores with accents).
main() writes report to fixed path 'runs/gui/report.json' without checking if file exists; could overwrite previous output.
compare() assumes reports[0]["metrics"] exists; crashes on empty reports list.
Metric.to_dict() truncates offenders to 12, but comment says 'every metric returns its count AND the elements behind it' — truncation may lose evidence.
